newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Six, including two children, killed in Tamil rebel land mine blast in eastern Polonnaruwa district.
Ruling People's Alliance and main opposition United National Party expected to nominate new people to contest March 27 local government elections.

About 50,000 policemen to be mobilised to ensure local government elections are peaceful, Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake says. Elections for local bodies are to be held throughout the country except in the north and east.
New Navy commander Vice Admiral Cecil Tissera takes over the reigns from outging commander Mohan Samarasekera.
Private sector must increase productivity by achieving good employer-employee relations, President Chandrika Kumaratunga tells a gathering of exporters.
Kumaratunga warns anyone found guilty of attempting to manipulate local government elections will be severely punished.
Sri Lanka's first wind power electricity project launched with French government aid.
